- [EBRT cost in India](/costs/India/Radiation-Oncology/EBRT)
Radiation Therapy vs Chemotherapy

| Feature | Radiation Therapy | Chemotherapy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Treatment type | Local | Systemic |
| Main target | Specific treatment area | Cancer cells throughout the body |
| Common breast cancer use | After surgery or selected metastatic sites | Before/after surgery or metastatic disease |
| Administration | External radiation or other specialized approaches | IV or oral medicines |
| Daily treatment | Often repeated sessions | Usually given in cycles |
| Main side effects | Often localized to treatment area | Can affect multiple body systems |

A patient may receive both because they serve different purposes. See [Chemotherapy for Breast Cancer in India](/blogs/chemotherapy-for-breast-cancer-in-india) and [Chemotherapy Cost in India](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Chemotherapy).
Radiation Therapy vs Surgery
Surgery physically removes the cancer. Radiation damages cancer cells in the treatment area. For breast cancer, the two are often complementary.

For example, [lumpectomy](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Lumpectomy) → radiation is a common treatment pathway for appropriately selected patients. [Mastectomy](/doctors/India/Surgical-Oncology/Mastectomy) may or may not be followed by radiation depending on pathology.
How Should Patients Prepare for Radiation Therapy?

items: Tell the team about previous radiation.
Tell the team about implants or reconstruction.
Inform the team about medications and medical conditions.
Plan transportation if daily travel is difficult.

blocks.text: Patients should not make major changes to their medication or diet without discussing them with their medical team.
Can International Patients Complete Radiation Therapy in India?

Yes, but radiation usually involves repeated visits over a period of time. International patients therefore need to plan accommodation near the hospital, transportation, treatment dates, attendant arrangements, follow-up appointments, emergency contact arrangements and travel home after treatment.

The exact duration depends on the prescribed radiation schedule. Hospitals in [Delhi NCR](/hospitals/India/Delhi-NCR), [Mumbai](/hospitals/India/Mumbai), [Bengaluru](/hospitals/India/Bengaluru), [Chennai](/hospitals/India/Chennai) and [Hyderabad](/hospitals/India/Hyderabad) can confirm start and completion dates before final travel arrangements.
What Records Should International Patients Send Before Travelling?

For a radiation opinion, useful records may include [pathology](/blogs/breast-cancer-diagnosis-tests-biopsy-er-pr-her2) (biopsy, histopathology, ER, PR, HER2 and other biomarkers), imaging (mammography, ultrasound, breast MRI, CT, PET-CT where applicable), surgery (operative report, final pathology, lymph-node pathology) and previous treatment (chemotherapy, targeted therapy and previous radiation records).
The radiation oncologist may request the actual imaging or pathology material if the available reports are insufficient.

Questions to Ask Your Radiation Oncologist

items: Will the lymph nodes be included?
How many sessions will I need?
What radiation technique will be used?
Can deep inspiration breath hold be used?
What side effects should I expect?
What skin-care instructions should I follow?
How long will each visit take?
What is included in the radiation cost estimate?

blocks.text: Frequently Asked Questions
Is radiation necessary after breast cancer surgery?
Not always. Radiation is commonly used after breast-conserving surgery and may be recommended after mastectomy depending on the patient's risk factors.
Do I need radiation after lumpectomy?
Many patients do, although selected low-risk patients may be able to omit it. The decision depends on the patient's age, tumour characteristics, pathology and overall treatment plan.
Do I need radiation after mastectomy?
Some patients do and others do not. Tumour size, lymph-node involvement, margins and other pathological findings can influence the recommendation.
How many radiation sessions are needed for breast cancer?
There is no universal number. The schedule depends on the treatment plan, cancer characteristics and radiation technique.
Is radiation therapy painful?
The radiation delivery itself is generally not painful. Side effects such as skin irritation, swelling or fatigue can develop during treatment.
Does radiation cause hair loss?
Radiation affects hair only in the area being treated. Breast radiation does not normally cause the type of whole-body hair loss associated with some chemotherapy medicines.
Can I work during radiation therapy?
Many patients continue some or all of their normal activities during radiation, although fatigue may increase as treatment progresses.
Can I travel while receiving radiation?
It may be possible, but patients receiving daily or frequent treatment need to remain close enough to the treatment centre. International travel should be planned with the radiation oncology team.
Can radiation be given after chemotherapy?
Yes. Chemotherapy and radiation can both be part of breast cancer treatment, and the sequence is determined by the oncology team.
Can radiation damage the heart?

Radiation to the left breast can expose part of the heart to radiation. Modern planning techniques aim to minimize this exposure, and techniques such as deep inspiration breath hold may be used for selected patients.
Can radiation affect breast reconstruction?

Yes. Radiation can influence reconstructed breast tissue and can affect reconstruction planning. The breast surgeon, reconstructive surgeon and radiation oncologist should coordinate when reconstruction is being considered.
How much does breast cancer radiation therapy cost in India?
There is no single fixed price. Cost depends on the radiation technique, number of sessions, treatment area, planning requirements, hospital and other factors.
Radiation Therapy for Breast Cancer in India: Key Takeaways

Radiation therapy is an important component of breast cancer treatment for many patients, particularly after breast-conserving surgery. It may also be recommended after mastectomy when the cancer has characteristics associated with a higher risk of local or regional recurrence.

The radiation plan depends on breast cancer stage, tumour size, lymph-node involvement, surgical margins, type of surgery, ER/PR/HER2 status, previous treatment, reconstruction and individual anatomy.

Modern radiation treatment is carefully planned to deliver radiation to the required area while limiting exposure to nearby healthy tissues. For international patients, radiation treatment requires additional planning because treatment may involve multiple hospital visits over several weeks or a shorter prescribed schedule.

The most useful next step is to have the complete pathology, imaging and surgical records reviewed by a radiation oncology team so that the treatment area, number of sessions, technique and estimated cost can be determined for the individual patient.

blocks.html:
Quick answer

Breast reconstruction after mastectomy is a surgical procedure used to rebuild the shape and appearance of the breast after breast cancer surgery. Reconstruction can be performed at the same time as mastectomy (immediate reconstruction) or months or years later (delayed reconstruction).

The main options include implant-based reconstruction and autologous reconstruction, which uses tissue from another part of the patient's body. Some patients may also undergo nipple-sparing mastectomy, allowing the nipple and surrounding skin to be preserved when medically appropriate.

The choice depends on factors such as the type and stage of breast cancer, planned radiation or chemotherapy, breast anatomy, overall health, previous surgeries, personal preferences and the reconstructive surgeon's assessment. Reconstruction may involve one or more operations, and recovery varies according to the technique used.

The cost of breast reconstruction in India varies considerably because it depends on the reconstruction technique, surgical complexity, hospital, implants or tissue-transfer requirements, investigations, length of stay and whether additional procedures are required. International patients should obtain a case-specific quotation after medical records and imaging have been reviewed.

blocks.text: A [mastectomy](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Mastectomy) removes some or all of the breast tissue as part of breast cancer treatment. Breast reconstruction is a surgical procedure that attempts to recreate the breast mound after this operation. This guide supports the [Breast Cancer Treatment in India](/treatments/breast-cancer-treatment-in-india) pathway and the [cost guide](/blogs/breast-cancer-treatment-cost-in-india).

blocks.label: Ask GAF about reconstruction timing

blocks.caption: Implant-based reconstruction uses an implant or a tissue expander. The alternative is autologous reconstruction using the patient's own tissue.

blocks.text: What Is Breast Reconstruction After Mastectomy?
Reconstruction can be performed during the same operation as mastectomy, after the mastectomy has healed, after completion of chemotherapy or radiation, or in stages over several months.
The goal is not to recreate a breast that is identical to the original breast. Instead, reconstruction aims to create a breast shape and contour that fits the patient's body and personal preferences.

Breast reconstruction is usually planned between the breast cancer surgeon and reconstructive/plastic surgeon. In some cases, radiation oncology and medical oncology are also involved because cancer treatment can affect when reconstruction should be performed. Teams in [Delhi NCR](/doctors/India/Delhi-NCR), [Mumbai](/doctors/India/Mumbai), [Bengaluru](/doctors/India/Bengaluru), [Chennai](/doctors/India/Chennai) and [Hyderabad](/doctors/India/Hyderabad) coordinate this as part of the broader treatment pathway rather than as an isolated cosmetic procedure.
Why Do Patients Consider Breast Reconstruction?

After mastectomy, some patients choose reconstruction because they want to restore breast shape or feel more comfortable with their body. Others may decide not to have reconstruction and instead use an external breast prosthesis or choose a flat closure.

There is no single reconstruction option that is appropriate for every patient. The decision may depend on cancer treatment requirements, type of mastectomy, whether radiation therapy is planned, breast size and shape, available tissue, previous abdominal or chest surgery, general health, smoking status, body weight, personal preferences, expected recovery time and willingness to undergo additional procedures.
Immediate vs Delayed Breast Reconstruction

blocks.alt: Two patients with a surgeon illustrating immediate versus delayed reconstruction timing
blocks.caption: Immediate reconstruction happens in the same operation as mastectomy. Delayed reconstruction waits until cancer treatment has progressed or finished.

blocks.text: Immediate Breast Reconstruction
Immediate reconstruction is performed during the same surgical session as the mastectomy — for example, mastectomy → reconstruction during the same operation.

Potential advantages include reconstructing the breast during the initial surgery, retaining more of the natural breast skin in some patients, avoiding a separate period without a reconstructed breast, and fewer separate major operations in selected cases.

However, immediate reconstruction is not suitable for everyone. If additional cancer treatment is expected, particularly [radiation therapy](/costs/India/Radiation-Oncology/EBRT), the timing and reconstruction technique require careful planning.
Delayed Breast Reconstruction

Delayed reconstruction is performed after the mastectomy. It may take place several months later, after [chemotherapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Chemotherapy), after radiation therapy, or after other cancer treatments have been completed.

Delayed reconstruction may be considered when the priority is completing cancer treatment first or when radiation could significantly influence the reconstruction strategy. The interval between mastectomy and reconstruction varies from patient to patient.

[Ask whether immediate or delayed reconstruction fits](/consult?treatment=Breast%20Reconstruction) · [WhatsApp +91 90443 46292](https://wa.me/919044346292?text=Should%20my%20reconstruction%20be%20immediate%20or%20delayed%20after%20mastectomy%3F)
What Are the Main Types of Breast Reconstruction?
Breast reconstruction generally falls into two broad categories: implant-based reconstruction and autologous or tissue-based reconstruction. Some patients undergo a combination of techniques.
1. Implant-Based Breast Reconstruction

Implant reconstruction uses a breast implant to create the reconstructed breast. In some cases, reconstruction can involve placement of an implant directly during surgery. In other cases, a tissue expander is initially used.
What Is a Tissue Expander?

A tissue expander is a temporary device used to gradually stretch the breast skin and surrounding tissues. The process may involve placement of the expander during surgery, gradual expansion over time, and replacement of the expander with a permanent implant during another procedure.

Potential advantages of implant-based reconstruction may include avoiding tissue from another part of the body, less extensive surgery than some tissue-transfer procedures, and a relatively predictable breast volume.

Potential limitations can include multiple procedures, implant-related complications, capsular contracture, infection, implant displacement and changes in breast appearance over time. Patients should discuss the expected lifespan of implants and the possibility of future procedures with their surgeon.
2. Autologous Breast Reconstruction

blocks.alt: Surgeon indicating a possible abdominal tissue-donor site on a clothed patient
blocks.caption: Autologous reconstruction uses the patient's own tissue, often from the abdomen, back or thigh. It is a longer operation with a donor-site scar.

blocks.text: Autologous reconstruction uses the patient's own tissue to create the reconstructed breast. The tissue may come from the abdomen, back, thigh or other suitable donor sites.

The tissue can be transferred while maintaining its blood supply or may be completely detached and reconnected to blood vessels using microsurgical techniques. One commonly discussed approach is abdominal tissue reconstruction.
Potential advantages can include a breast made from the patient's own tissue, a more natural tissue feel in some patients, and no permanent breast implant.

Because tissue is taken from another part of the body, the procedure can involve a longer operation, a donor-site scar, longer recovery, additional surgical risks and more complex postoperative monitoring. Not every patient has sufficient tissue or is medically suitable for this type of reconstruction.
Implant vs Autologous Reconstruction

| Feature | Implant-Based | Autologous Reconstruction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main material | Breast implant | Patient's own tissue |
| Donor site required | No | Yes |
| Surgical complexity | Often lower, depending on case | Often more complex |
| Multiple procedures | May be required | May be required |
| Recovery | Depends on technique | Often longer |
| Effect of radiation | Important consideration | Also important |
| Suitable for everyone | No | No |

blocks.text: Can Breast Reconstruction Be Done With Nipple-Sparing Mastectomy?

In selected patients, breast reconstruction can be performed alongside [nipple-sparing mastectomy](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Nipple-Sparing-Mastectomy). During nipple-sparing mastectomy, breast tissue is removed while the nipple-areola complex and some of the surrounding breast skin are preserved.

This can potentially provide a more natural breast appearance after reconstruction. However, nipple-sparing surgery is not appropriate for every breast cancer patient. Factors considered may include tumour location, tumour involvement near the nipple, breast anatomy, cancer characteristics, surgical assessment and patient-specific risk factors.

- [Nipple-Sparing Mastectomy Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Surgical-Oncology/Nipple-Sparing-Mastectomy)
- [Nipple-Sparing Mastectomy Cost](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Nipple-Sparing-Mastectomy)
Breast Reconstruction and Oncoplastic Surgery: Are They the Same?

[Oncoplastic breast surgery](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Oncoplastic-Breast-Surgery) combines cancer surgery with plastic-surgery principles to reshape the breast after removal of the tumour. It is commonly associated with [breast-conserving surgery](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Lumpectomy), although reconstructive techniques can be used in different breast cancer operations.

Breast reconstruction after mastectomy, on the other hand, generally involves rebuilding the breast after most or all of the breast tissue has been removed. Both approaches aim to achieve an appropriate cancer operation while considering breast appearance and body shape.

- [Oncoplastic Breast Surgery Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Surgical-Oncology/Oncoplastic-Breast-Surgery)
- [Oncoplastic Breast Surgery Cost](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Oncoplastic-Breast-Surgery)
How Does Radiation Therapy Affect Breast Reconstruction?

Radiation therapy is an important factor when planning reconstruction. Radiation can affect the skin and underlying tissues and may influence healing and the final appearance of a reconstructed breast.

For this reason, the treatment team may discuss whether radiation is required, whether reconstruction should be immediate or delayed, which reconstructive technique may be appropriate, and whether additional procedures could be needed later. There is no universal rule. This is particularly important for patients who require [post-mastectomy radiation](/costs/India/Radiation-Oncology/EBRT).
What Happens Before Breast Reconstruction?

Before surgery, the medical team usually reviews the patient's complete cancer and treatment history. This may include [diagnosis](/blogs/breast-cancer-diagnosis-tests-biopsy-er-pr-her2) records — biopsy reports, histopathology, tumour characteristics, [ER, PR and HER2 status](/blogs/er-pr-her2-breast-cancer-treatment-india), imaging and [cancer stage](/blogs/breast-cancer-stages-0-1-2-3-4).

Doctors may also need information about previous breast surgery, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, hormone therapy, targeted treatment, other medical conditions and previous abdominal or chest operations.

The reconstructive surgeon evaluates breast size and shape, skin availability, chest-wall anatomy, available donor tissue and scarring from previous procedures. If radiation or additional systemic treatment is expected, these factors are incorporated into the reconstruction plan.
What Happens During Breast Reconstruction?
The exact operation depends on the reconstruction technique.

**Implant-based reconstruction:** mastectomy → implant or tissue expander placement → healing → further expansion or implant exchange if required. Some patients may need additional procedures to improve symmetry.

**Autologous reconstruction:** mastectomy → tissue harvested from donor area → tissue transferred to the chest → blood vessels connected where required → breast shaped and reconstructed. The actual procedure is considerably more detailed and varies between reconstructive techniques.
How Long Does Recovery Take?

blocks.alt: International patient with a suitcase and discharge folder during a postoperative dressing check
blocks.caption: Recovery and travel clearance depend on the technique. Tissue-based reconstruction usually needs a longer stay than a straightforward implant procedure.

blocks.text: Recovery depends heavily on the type of reconstruction. A straightforward implant-based reconstruction may have a different recovery pathway from a complex tissue-transfer operation.

During recovery, patients may experience pain or tightness, swelling, bruising, temporary changes in sensation, reduced physical activity, incision discomfort and fatigue. Patients undergoing tissue-based reconstruction may also need to recover from the donor-site operation.
The surgeon will provide specific instructions regarding wound care, physical activity, lifting restrictions, exercise, driving, work and follow-up appointments.
Possible Complications of Breast Reconstruction

Like other major surgical procedures, breast reconstruction carries risks. Potential complications may include infection, bleeding, fluid accumulation, wound-healing problems, scarring, changes in sensation, asymmetry, implant-related complications, capsular contracture, tissue loss in flap reconstruction, donor-site complications and the need for additional surgery.
The actual risk varies according to the technique, patient factors and other cancer treatments. Patients should discuss procedure-specific risks with the reconstructive surgeon before surgery.
Will the Reconstructed Breast Feel the Same?
Usually, a reconstructed breast does not feel exactly the same as the original breast. Sensation can change substantially after mastectomy because breast tissue and nerves are removed or altered.
Some patients experience numbness, reduced sensation, altered sensitivity, tightness or gradual changes in sensation over time. The final appearance and feel also depend on the reconstruction method.
Can Breast Reconstruction Be Done Years After Mastectomy?

Yes. Delayed breast reconstruction can be performed months or even years after mastectomy in appropriately selected patients. A patient who previously chose not to undergo reconstruction can discuss reconstructive options later.

The reconstructive plan may be influenced by previous radiation, previous surgery, scar tissue, available tissue, current health and cancer history. A new surgical assessment is required before proceeding.
Does Breast Reconstruction Treat Breast Cancer?
No. Breast reconstruction is intended to restore breast shape after cancer surgery. It does not replace cancer treatment.

Breast cancer treatment may involve [surgery](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Mastectomy), [chemotherapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Chemotherapy), [radiation therapy](/costs/India/Radiation-Oncology/EBRT), [hormone therapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Hormone-Therapy), [targeted therapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Targeted-Therapy) and [immunotherapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Immunotherapy). The cancer treatment plan always takes priority when determining reconstruction timing. See [Breast Cancer Treatment in India](/treatments/breast-cancer-treatment-in-india).
Breast Reconstruction After Mastectomy: What About Radiation and Chemotherapy?

**Chemotherapy** may be given before or after surgery depending on the cancer subtype and [treatment-by-stage](/blogs/breast-cancer-treatment-by-stage) plan. If chemotherapy is planned, the timing of reconstruction needs to be coordinated with systemic treatment.

**Radiation** may be recommended after mastectomy for selected patients. Because radiation can affect reconstructed tissues, the reconstructive surgeon and radiation oncologist should coordinate treatment planning.

**Hormone therapy** for [hormone receptor-positive](/blogs/hormone-therapy-breast-cancer-india) disease generally does not require the same surgical scheduling considerations as chemotherapy or radiation, but the overall cancer treatment plan remains relevant. [HER2-positive](/blogs/her2-positive-breast-cancer-treatment-india) disease may add targeted therapy to the sequence.
How Much Does Breast Reconstruction Cost in India?

There is no single fixed price for breast reconstruction in India. The final cost can vary substantially. See [Breast Reconstruction Cost in India](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Breast-Reconstruction) and the [breast cancer treatment cost guide](/blogs/breast-cancer-treatment-cost-in-india).

Major cost factors may include the type of reconstruction, implant or tissue-expander requirements, autologous tissue-transfer technique, surgical complexity, hospital charges, surgeon and specialist fees, anaesthesia, diagnostic investigations, medicines, length of hospital stay, additional procedures, follow-up treatment and management of complications if they occur.

blocks.text: [WhatsApp +91 90443 46292 for a case-specific quote](https://wa.me/919044346292?text=Please%20send%20a%20case-specific%20quotation%20for%20breast%20reconstruction%20after%20mastectomy%20in%20India.)
Breast Reconstruction Cost vs Mastectomy Cost

These are not necessarily the same surgical expense. A [mastectomy](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Mastectomy) is the cancer-removal operation. Breast reconstruction is an additional reconstructive procedure that may be performed during the same operation or separately.

Depending on the treatment plan, a patient may therefore receive a quotation covering mastectomy, reconstruction, hospitalization, anaesthesia, implants or reconstructive materials, diagnostic tests and postoperative care. Patients should ask hospitals to clearly explain what is included.

- [Mastectomy Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Surgical-Oncology/Mastectomy)
- [Mastectomy Cost in India](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Mastectomy)
Breast Reconstruction for International Patients

India is a treatment destination for international patients seeking breast cancer surgery and reconstructive procedures. Preparation is particularly important because reconstruction may involve significant recovery time. See the [international-patient guide](/blogs/breast-cancer-treatment-india-international-patients).

Before travelling, patients should ideally provide the biopsy report, histopathology, ER/PR/HER2 results, imaging reports and files, previous surgery records, chemotherapy and radiation records, medication list and medical history.

The patient may meet a breast surgical oncologist, reconstructive/plastic surgeon, medical oncologist, radiation oncologist, radiologist and pathologist. Hospitals in [Delhi NCR](/hospitals/India/Delhi-NCR), [Mumbai](/hospitals/India/Mumbai), [Bengaluru](/hospitals/India/Bengaluru), [Chennai](/hospitals/India/Chennai) and [Hyderabad](/hospitals/India/Hyderabad) can confirm what to send.

International patients should allow sufficient time for the initial postoperative review, wound assessment, drain management where applicable, recovery and travel clearance. The exact duration should be determined by the treating team rather than relying on a standard number of days.

[WhatsApp +91 90443 46292 your records before travel](https://wa.me/919044346292?text=I%20would%20like%20to%20send%20my%20mastectomy%20and%20reconstruction%20records%20for%20review%20before%20travelling%20to%20India.)
How to Choose a Breast Reconstruction Team in India

Patients comparing hospitals should look beyond the reconstruction procedure itself. Important questions include whether the hospital has a multidisciplinary breast cancer team, whether the surgical team performs the required reconstruction technique, how radiation will affect the plan, what is included in the quotation, and what happens if another procedure is required.

Ask specifically about the procedure being considered rather than simply asking whether a hospital performs "breast reconstruction." Some reconstruction pathways involve staged procedures. Understanding this before treatment can help patients plan both financially and logistically.
Questions to Ask the Reconstructive Surgeon

items: Am I medically suitable for breast reconstruction?
Would delayed reconstruction be more appropriate?
Which reconstruction techniques are suitable for me?
Would an implant or my own tissue be more appropriate?
Will I need more than one operation?
What complications should I know about?
How will reconstruction affect future breast cancer follow-up?
What costs are included in the treatment quotation?

blocks.text: Frequently Asked Questions
Can breast reconstruction be done at the same time as mastectomy?
Yes. Immediate reconstruction can be performed during the same operation as mastectomy in selected patients.
Can reconstruction be performed after radiation therapy?
Yes. Reconstruction can be performed after radiation, although previous radiation can affect tissue quality and influence the choice of reconstruction technique.
Is breast reconstruction mandatory after mastectomy?
No. Some patients choose reconstruction, while others prefer an external prosthesis or a flat closure.
Is breast reconstruction considered cosmetic surgery?

In the context of breast cancer treatment, reconstruction is generally performed to restore the breast following cancer surgery. It should be considered as part of the overall cancer treatment and recovery plan.
Which is better: implants or tissue reconstruction?
There is no single option that is appropriate for everyone. The decision depends on anatomy, cancer treatment, radiation, health, available tissue and personal preferences.
Can reconstruction be performed after nipple-sparing mastectomy?
Yes. Nipple-sparing mastectomy is commonly considered in conjunction with reconstruction when the patient meets the appropriate criteria.
Will the reconstructed breast have normal sensation?
Sensation is often altered after mastectomy and reconstruction. Numbness or reduced sensation can occur.
Does breast reconstruction increase the risk of breast cancer coming back?
Reconstruction itself is not a substitute for cancer treatment. Decisions about recurrence risk and follow-up depend on the original cancer and its treatment.
How many surgeries are required?
Some patients complete reconstruction in one operation, while others require staged procedures. The number depends on the reconstruction technique and individual circumstances.
How much does breast reconstruction cost in India?
There is no universal price. The cost depends on the reconstruction technique, hospital, surgical complexity, implants or tissue-transfer requirements, investigations and other treatment factors.
Can international patients undergo breast reconstruction in India?

Yes, international patients can seek breast reconstruction in India. Their medical records should ideally be reviewed before travel so the treating team can plan consultation, investigations and treatment.
Can breast reconstruction be done years after mastectomy?
Yes. Delayed reconstruction may be considered months or years after mastectomy, depending on the patient's health, previous treatments and reconstructive options.
Breast Reconstruction After Mastectomy in India: Key Takeaways

Breast reconstruction is an important option for patients who have undergone or are planning mastectomy for breast cancer. The main approaches are implant-based reconstruction, tissue-based/autologous reconstruction, immediate reconstruction and delayed reconstruction.

The decision is influenced by cancer treatment, radiation requirements, breast anatomy, available tissue, overall health and personal preferences. For international patients, it is particularly important to have pathology, imaging and previous treatment records reviewed before travelling.

blocks.html:
Quick answer

Hormone therapy, also called endocrine therapy, is used for breast cancers that have hormone receptors, particularly estrogen receptor (ER)-positive and/or progesterone receptor (PR)-positive cancers. It works by reducing the effect of estrogen or progesterone on cancer cells and can be used before or after other treatments depending on the individual cancer plan.

Common hormone therapy medicines include tamoxifen and aromatase inhibitors such as anastrozole, letrozole and exemestane. Some patients may also receive ovarian-function suppression or other endocrine treatments.

Hormone therapy may be recommended after surgery to reduce the risk of recurrence, and it can also be used in advanced or metastatic hormone receptor-positive breast cancer. The choice of treatment depends on menopausal status, tumour biology, previous treatment, recurrence risk, other medical conditions and the overall treatment plan.

Treatment duration can extend for several years, although the exact duration varies between patients. The cost in India depends on the medicine, duration, monitoring and whether other treatments are required.

blocks.text: Hormone therapy is a type of systemic treatment for breast cancer. Unlike [surgery](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Lumpectomy) or [radiation therapy](/costs/India/Radiation-Oncology/EBRT), which primarily target specific areas of the body, hormone therapy works throughout the body. This guide supports the [Breast Cancer Treatment in India](/treatments/breast-cancer-treatment-in-india) pathway, the [ER, PR and HER2 explainer](/blogs/er-pr-her2-breast-cancer-treatment-india) and the [cost guide](/blogs/breast-cancer-treatment-cost-in-india).

blocks.label: Ask GAF whether hormone therapy applies

blocks.text: [WhatsApp +91 90443 46292 with your ER/PR report](https://wa.me/919044346292?text=Please%20review%20my%20ER%2FPR%20report%20for%20hormone%20therapy%20in%20India.)

blocks.alt: Adult torso beside a magnified estrogen-receptor diagram being blocked by endocrine tablets
blocks.caption: Hormone therapy does not add hormones. It blocks estrogen's effect or lowers estrogen production so receptor-positive cells are less able to grow.

blocks.text: What Is Hormone Therapy for Breast Cancer?
It is mainly used when breast cancer cells depend on hormones such as estrogen or progesterone to grow. The treatment is also called endocrine therapy, hormonal therapy or anti-hormonal therapy.

Despite the name, hormone therapy for breast cancer does not mean giving hormones to treat cancer. Instead, it generally works by blocking the action of estrogen, lowering estrogen levels, or preventing estrogen from stimulating cancer cells.

Oncology teams in [Delhi NCR](/doctors/India/Delhi-NCR), [Mumbai](/doctors/India/Mumbai), [Bengaluru](/doctors/India/Bengaluru), [Chennai](/doctors/India/Chennai) and [Hyderabad](/doctors/India/Hyderabad) use ER and PR results together with [stage](/blogs/breast-cancer-stages-0-1-2-3-4) and [HER2 status](/blogs/her2-positive-breast-cancer-treatment-india) to decide whether endocrine treatment belongs in the plan.
Who Needs Hormone Therapy for Breast Cancer?

Hormone therapy is generally considered when testing shows that the cancer is hormone receptor-positive. Breast cancer pathology commonly includes testing for estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR) and [HER2](/blogs/er-pr-her2-breast-cancer-treatment-india).

A tumour may therefore be described as ER-positive, PR-positive, ER-positive/PR-positive or hormone receptor-positive. The pathology report helps the oncology team determine whether endocrine therapy is likely to be useful.

If a tumour does not express hormone receptors, hormone therapy generally does not form the same role in treatment. This is why [pathology and receptor testing](/blogs/breast-cancer-diagnosis-tests-biopsy-er-pr-her2) are critical parts of breast cancer treatment planning.
How Does Hormone Therapy Work?
Hormone therapy can work through different mechanisms. The two major approaches are:

items: Blocking the effect of estrogen — some medicines attach to estrogen receptors and interfere with estrogen's ability to stimulate cancer cells.
Reducing estrogen production — other medicines reduce the amount of estrogen produced by the body.

blocks.text: The appropriate approach depends partly on whether the patient is premenopausal or postmenopausal.
Common Hormone Therapy Medicines

blocks.alt: Patient and medical oncologist reviewing a tablet blister pack and pathology folder
blocks.caption: The medicine chosen — tamoxifen, an aromatase inhibitor, or ovarian-function suppression — depends on menopausal status and the rest of the pathology.

blocks.text: Tamoxifen

Tamoxifen is a selective estrogen receptor modulator, commonly known as a SERM. It works by blocking estrogen's effects in breast tissue. Tamoxifen can be used in both premenopausal and postmenopausal patients, although the overall treatment strategy varies according to the patient's circumstances.
Aromatase Inhibitors

Common aromatase inhibitors include anastrozole, letrozole and exemestane. These medicines reduce estrogen production in the body. They are commonly used in postmenopausal patients. In some premenopausal patients, an aromatase inhibitor may be used together with ovarian-function suppression.
Ovarian-Function Suppression

For some premenopausal patients, doctors may recommend treatment that suppresses ovarian estrogen production. This can be combined with endocrine medicines depending on the individual's cancer characteristics and treatment plan.
The decision depends on age, menopausal status, tumour characteristics, recurrence risk, previous treatments and tolerance of treatment.

- [Hormone Therapy Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Medical-Oncology/Hormone-Therapy)
- [Hormone Therapy Cost in India](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Hormone-Therapy)

[Ask which endocrine medicine applies](/consult?treatment=Hormone%20Therapy) · [WhatsApp +91 90443 46292](https://wa.me/919044346292?text=Which%20hormone%20therapy%20medicine%20is%20appropriate%20for%20my%20ER%2FPR-positive%20breast%20cancer%3F)
Hormone Therapy Before or After Surgery
Hormone therapy can be incorporated into breast cancer treatment at different points.
Before Surgery

In selected patients, endocrine therapy may be considered before surgery. This approach is called neoadjuvant endocrine therapy. It may be used in specific clinical situations, particularly for some hormone receptor-positive cancers. However, it is not required for every patient.
After Surgery

Hormone therapy is frequently used as adjuvant treatment for appropriate hormone receptor-positive breast cancers. The objective is to reduce the risk that cancer cells remaining elsewhere in the body could grow in the future.

Depending on the individual treatment plan, endocrine therapy may be given after [breast-conserving surgery](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Lumpectomy), [mastectomy](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Mastectomy), [chemotherapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Chemotherapy) or [radiation therapy](/costs/India/Radiation-Oncology/EBRT). The sequence can vary.
Hormone Therapy for Early-Stage Breast Cancer

For early-stage hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, treatment may involve several components. A typical pathway might include: Diagnosis → Surgery → Pathology → Risk assessment → Additional treatment → Hormone therapy. See [treatment by stage](/blogs/breast-cancer-treatment-by-stage).
Depending on the individual case, additional treatments may include radiation therapy, chemotherapy and targeted therapy. Not every patient needs all of these treatments.
Hormone Therapy for Advanced or Metastatic Breast Cancer

Hormone therapy can also be an important treatment for hormone receptor-positive advanced or metastatic breast cancer. In this setting, treatment is usually aimed at controlling the disease, slowing progression and maintaining quality of life for as long as possible.

Endocrine therapy may be combined with other systemic medicines depending on the cancer's characteristics and previous treatment. Treatment selection can change over time if the cancer stops responding to a particular therapy.
Hormone Therapy for Premenopausal Women

blocks.alt: Clinician with a younger patient holding an injection pen and an older patient holding a tablet pack
blocks.caption: Premenopausal treatment may include tamoxifen or ovarian-function suppression. Postmenopausal treatment more often uses an aromatase inhibitor.

blocks.text: Menopausal status is important when selecting endocrine treatment. In premenopausal women, the ovaries continue producing significant amounts of estrogen.

Therefore, treatment may involve tamoxifen, ovarian-function suppression, or ovarian-function suppression plus an aromatase inhibitor. The appropriate approach depends on the patient's individual risk profile and treatment goals.
It is important not to select hormone therapy based only on age. Menopausal status and ovarian function need to be considered by the treating oncologist.
Hormone Therapy for Postmenopausal Women

Postmenopausal women generally have lower ovarian estrogen production. Aromatase inhibitors are commonly used in this setting. Possible medicines include anastrozole, letrozole and exemestane. Tamoxifen may also have a role in some treatment plans.
The choice depends on the patient's cancer characteristics, previous treatment, medical history and tolerance.
How Long Is Hormone Therapy Given?
Hormone therapy is usually a long-term treatment. Many patients receive endocrine therapy for several years. However, the exact duration is individualized.

Factors that may influence duration include cancer stage, tumour biology, recurrence risk, menopausal status, previous endocrine treatment, treatment tolerance and risk of recurrence over time. Some patients may change from one endocrine medicine to another during treatment.

blocks.label: WhatsApp +91 90443 46292 about treatment duration

blocks.text: What Are the Side Effects of Hormone Therapy?
Side effects vary according to the medicine. Some patients experience relatively mild symptoms, while others may find certain side effects more difficult to tolerate.

Common side effects can include hot flashes, night sweats, joint or muscle discomfort, fatigue, mood changes, vaginal dryness and changes in sexual health. The side-effect profile differs between tamoxifen and aromatase inhibitors.
Tamoxifen: Important Side Effects

Tamoxifen can cause symptoms such as hot flashes, night sweats, vaginal symptoms, menstrual changes and mood changes. Rare but important risks can include blood clots and certain changes in the lining of the uterus. Patients should discuss their individual risk factors with their oncologist.
Aromatase Inhibitors: Important Side Effects

Aromatase inhibitors can commonly cause joint pain, muscle discomfort, hot flashes, stiffness and fatigue. Long-term treatment may also affect bone health in some patients. For patients taking aromatase inhibitors, doctors may monitor bone health and recommend appropriate measures based on individual risk.
Does Hormone Therapy Cause Menopause?
Hormone therapy can cause or intensify menopausal symptoms. This is particularly relevant for premenopausal patients receiving ovarian-function suppression.

Symptoms may include hot flashes, sweating, changes in menstrual periods, vaginal dryness, changes in sexual function and mood changes. However, the exact experience varies significantly between patients.
Can Hormone Therapy Be Stopped Because of Side Effects?

Patients should not stop endocrine therapy on their own. If side effects become difficult to manage, the oncology team may consider changing the medication, adjusting the treatment strategy, managing individual symptoms, or switching between endocrine therapies when medically appropriate.
The goal is to maintain effective cancer treatment while making long-term therapy as manageable as possible.
Hormone Therapy vs Chemotherapy

| Feature | Hormone Therapy | Chemotherapy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main mechanism | Targets hormone signalling | Uses anticancer drugs to damage/kill cancer cells |
| Main use | Hormone receptor-positive cancers | Used for selected breast cancers |
| Treatment | Usually long-term | Often given in defined cycles |
| Administration | Often oral; some treatments injectable | Usually intravenous, sometimes oral depending on regimen |
| Side effects | Often endocrine-related | Can include fatigue, nausea, hair loss, blood-count changes and others |
| Applicability | Depends strongly on ER/PR status | Depends on tumour characteristics and clinical risk |
Some patients receive both. Others may not require [chemotherapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Chemotherapy) but may still receive hormone therapy.

- [Chemotherapy Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Medical-Oncology/Chemotherapy)
- [Chemotherapy Cost in India](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Chemotherapy)
Hormone Therapy vs Targeted Therapy

[Targeted therapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Targeted-Therapy) is different from endocrine therapy. For example, [HER2-targeted medicines](/blogs/her2-positive-breast-cancer-treatment-india) are designed to interfere with HER2-driven cancer biology. Hormone therapy, in contrast, targets hormone signalling.
A patient can sometimes receive both approaches if the cancer has characteristics that make both treatments appropriate.

- [Targeted Therapy Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Medical-Oncology/Targeted-Therapy)
- [Targeted Therapy Cost in India](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Targeted-Therapy)
Hormone Therapy vs Immunotherapy

[Immunotherapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Immunotherapy) works by helping the immune system recognize or attack cancer cells through specific immune mechanisms. It is different from endocrine treatment.

Whether immunotherapy has a role depends on the biological characteristics of the breast cancer and the patient's clinical situation. Therefore, hormone therapy should not be considered interchangeable with immunotherapy.

- [Immunotherapy Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Medical-Oncology/Immunotherapy)
- [Immunotherapy Cost in India](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Immunotherapy)
Can Hormone Therapy Be Combined With Radiation?

Yes. Radiation therapy and endocrine therapy work differently and may both form part of treatment for appropriate patients. For example, a patient undergoing breast-conserving surgery may receive lumpectomy → [radiation therapy](/costs/India/Radiation-Oncology/EBRT) → hormone therapy. The actual sequence varies according to the treatment plan.
What Tests Are Needed Before Hormone Therapy?
The treatment team generally needs a confirmed diagnosis and [pathology assessment](/blogs/breast-cancer-diagnosis-tests-biopsy-er-pr-her2) before selecting endocrine therapy.

Important information may include histopathology, ER status, PR status, HER2 status, tumour grade, cancer stage, lymph-node status, menopausal status, previous cancer treatment and other medical conditions. Additional tests may be recommended depending on the treatment being considered.
Why ER and PR Testing Matters
ER and PR testing provides important information about whether breast cancer cells have hormone receptors. A positive hormone receptor result can influence the treatment plan.

For international patients seeking treatment in India, it is therefore useful to bring the complete pathology report, rather than only a summary diagnosis. If possible, patients should also bring the original pathology slides or blocks when their treating hospital requests them for review. See the [international-patient guide](/blogs/breast-cancer-treatment-india-international-patients).
What Happens During Follow-Up?

Hormone therapy usually involves long-term follow-up. During appointments, doctors may review medication adherence, side effects, menopausal symptoms, bone health where relevant, other medicines, new symptoms and overall cancer follow-up.
Patients should tell their doctor about persistent or severe symptoms rather than discontinuing treatment independently.
Hormone Therapy and Bone Health

blocks.alt: Patient on a medical imaging table during follow-up monitoring while a clinician reviews the scan
blocks.caption: Aromatase inhibitors can affect bone health in some patients, so follow-up may include bone-density assessment and other monitoring.

blocks.text: Bone health can be particularly relevant for patients taking aromatase inhibitors. Estrogen has an important role in maintaining bone strength. Reducing estrogen levels can therefore contribute to bone loss in some patients.

Depending on individual risk, doctors may consider bone-density assessment, calcium and vitamin D intake, weight-bearing physical activity, lifestyle measures and medicines to protect bone health when appropriate.
Hormone Therapy and Fertility

Fertility can be an important consideration for younger patients. Because endocrine therapy can last for several years, women who may want future pregnancies should discuss fertility and treatment timing with their oncology team before starting treatment.
Fertility preservation may need to be considered before certain cancer treatments. The approach must be individualized because cancer treatment should not be delayed inappropriately.
Hormone Therapy for International Patients in India
International patients considering breast cancer treatment in India should ideally have their pathology and treatment records reviewed before travelling.

items: Previous surgery, chemotherapy and radiation records
Current medication list and previous endocrine therapy details

blocks.text: A patient already taking hormone therapy should bring the exact medicine name, dose and duration. Hospitals in [Delhi NCR](/hospitals/India/Delhi-NCR), [Mumbai](/hospitals/India/Mumbai), [Bengaluru](/hospitals/India/Bengaluru), [Chennai](/hospitals/India/Chennai) and [Hyderabad](/hospitals/India/Hyderabad) can confirm what to send.

[WhatsApp +91 90443 46292 your records before travel](https://wa.me/919044346292?text=I%20would%20like%20to%20send%20my%20hormone-receptor%20reports%20for%20review%20before%20travelling%20to%20India.)
What Determines the Cost of Hormone Therapy in India?

Hormone therapy can be considerably different from surgery or chemotherapy because many endocrine medicines are taken over a long period. See [Hormone Therapy Cost in India](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Hormone-Therapy) and the [breast cancer treatment cost guide](/blogs/breast-cancer-treatment-cost-in-india).

The overall cost may depend on the medicine selected, brand or formulation, treatment duration, ovarian-function suppression if required, follow-up consultations, monitoring tests, bone-density monitoring where appropriate, and other medicines used alongside endocrine therapy.
There is therefore no single cost applicable to every patient. For a personalized estimate, the treatment plan and medication requirements should be reviewed by the treating oncology team.

blocks.label: Request a hormone-therapy quotation

blocks.text: How Much Does Hormone Therapy Cost Compared With Chemotherapy?

The two treatments have very different cost structures. Chemotherapy often involves multiple treatment cycles, hospital or day-care administration, pre-treatment tests, medicines administered during each cycle, supportive medicines and periodic monitoring.

Hormone therapy may involve a medicine taken over an extended period, with regular follow-up. Therefore, comparing a single chemotherapy cycle with a full course of endocrine treatment does not provide a meaningful picture of total treatment expense. Patients should ask for a treatment-specific quotation based on the prescribed regimen.
Questions to Ask Your Oncologist About Hormone Therapy

items: Is my breast cancer hormone receptor-positive?
What are my ER and PR results?
Am I premenopausal or postmenopausal for treatment purposes?
Which endocrine therapy is being recommended?
Why is this particular medicine being selected?
How long will I need to take it?
What side effects should I expect?
How can side effects be managed?
How does hormone therapy fit with chemotherapy or radiation?
What should I do if I miss a dose?
What follow-up tests will I need?

blocks.text: Frequently Asked Questions
What is hormone therapy for breast cancer?
Hormone therapy is systemic treatment used mainly for hormone receptor-positive breast cancer. It reduces the effect or production of hormones that can stimulate cancer cells.
Who needs hormone therapy?
It is generally considered for patients whose breast cancer expresses hormone receptors, particularly ER and/or PR.
Is hormone therapy the same as chemotherapy?
No. They work through different mechanisms. Hormone therapy targets hormone signalling, while chemotherapy uses anticancer drugs that act through different mechanisms.
Is hormone therapy given before or after surgery?

It can be used at different stages of treatment. For many patients with early-stage hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, it is given as adjuvant treatment after surgery, but treatment sequencing varies.
How long do I need hormone therapy?
Treatment commonly lasts for several years, but the duration depends on individual cancer characteristics, recurrence risk, menopausal status, previous treatment and tolerance.
Can men receive hormone therapy for breast cancer?
Yes. Breast cancer can occur in men, and hormone receptor-positive breast cancer in men may be treated with endocrine therapy when clinically appropriate.
Does hormone therapy cause hair loss?
Hair loss is not generally the same type of prominent side effect associated with some chemotherapy regimens. However, individual medicines can have different side-effect profiles.
Can hormone therapy be taken with chemotherapy?
Yes. Depending on the treatment plan, endocrine therapy may be part of a broader treatment strategy that also includes chemotherapy.
Can hormone therapy be combined with targeted therapy?
Yes. Some hormone receptor-positive cancers may also have other biological characteristics that make targeted therapy appropriate.
What happens if hormone therapy causes severe side effects?

Speak with the treating oncologist. Depending on the situation, the doctor may manage the symptoms or consider a different endocrine treatment. Patients should not stop treatment without medical advice.
Is hormone therapy used for triple-negative breast cancer?
Triple-negative breast cancer does not express estrogen or progesterone receptors, so endocrine therapy generally does not have the same role as it does in hormone receptor-positive breast cancer.
How much does hormone therapy cost in India?
The cost varies according to the medicine, treatment duration, monitoring and whether additional endocrine treatments such as ovarian-function suppression are required.
Hormone Therapy for Breast Cancer in India: Key Takeaways

Hormone therapy is an important component of treatment for many patients with hormone receptor-positive breast cancer. The treatment plan depends on ER and PR status, HER2 status, cancer stage, menopausal status, recurrence risk, previous treatment, other medical conditions, and patient preferences and treatment tolerance.

Common endocrine treatments include tamoxifen and aromatase inhibitors, while selected premenopausal patients may also receive ovarian-function suppression. Because hormone therapy can continue for several years, understanding both its benefits and possible side effects is important before starting treatment.
For patients seeking breast cancer treatment in India, the endocrine treatment plan should be integrated with surgery, chemotherapy, radiation and other systemic treatments where appropriate.

blocks.html:
Quick answer

HER2-positive breast cancer is a type of breast cancer in which cancer cells have higher-than-normal levels of the HER2 protein or gene activity. HER2 testing is performed on the tumour tissue and is an important part of treatment planning.

Treatment may include surgery, chemotherapy, HER2-targeted therapy, radiation therapy, hormone therapy, or a combination of these, depending on the cancer stage and other tumour characteristics.

Common HER2-targeted treatments include medicines such as trastuzumab and pertuzumab, while other HER2-directed medicines may be used in specific situations, including recurrent or metastatic disease.

HER2-positive breast cancer can also be hormone receptor-positive. When that happens, both HER2-targeted treatment and hormone therapy may have a role.

The cost of treatment in India varies significantly depending on the stage, treatment regimen, medicines used, number of cycles, hospital, surgery, radiation and follow-up requirements. A case-specific treatment plan and quotation are therefore necessary rather than relying on a single standard price.

blocks.text: HER2-positive breast cancer is breast cancer in which the tumour shows overexpression of the HER2 protein or amplification of the HER2 gene. This guide supports the [Breast Cancer Treatment in India](/treatments/breast-cancer-treatment-in-india) pathway, the [ER, PR and HER2 explainer](/blogs/er-pr-her2-breast-cancer-treatment-india), the [diagnosis guide](/blogs/breast-cancer-diagnosis-tests-biopsy-er-pr-her2) and the [cost guide](/blogs/breast-cancer-treatment-cost-in-india).

blocks.label: Ask GAF to review your HER2 report

blocks.text: [WhatsApp +91 90443 46292 with your HER2 report](https://wa.me/919044346292?text=Please%20review%20my%20HER2-positive%20breast%20cancer%20report%20for%20treatment%20in%20India.)

blocks.alt: Adult torso beside a magnified cell-membrane diagram of HER2 spikes being blocked by Y-shaped targeted medicines
blocks.caption: HER2 sits on the cell surface. Targeted medicines are designed to interfere with that signalling, which is why the pathology result matters.

blocks.text: What Is HER2-Positive Breast Cancer?
HER2 stands for human epidermal growth factor receptor 2. HER2 is a protein involved in cell growth and signalling.

When a breast cancer has abnormally high HER2 activity, it can influence how the cancer behaves and can also create an opportunity for HER2-targeted treatment. This is why HER2 testing has become an important part of breast cancer diagnosis and treatment planning.

Multidisciplinary teams in [Delhi NCR](/doctors/India/Delhi-NCR), [Mumbai](/doctors/India/Mumbai), [Bengaluru](/doctors/India/Bengaluru), [Chennai](/doctors/India/Chennai) and [Hyderabad](/doctors/India/Hyderabad) use HER2 results together with stage and ER/PR status to plan treatment.
What Does HER2 Positive Mean?
A pathology report may contain a HER2 result based on different tests. The most common initial test is immunohistochemistry (IHC).
Results may be reported as HER2 0, HER2 1+, HER2 2+ or HER2 3+.

A result of 3+ on IHC is generally considered HER2-positive. A result of 2+ is usually considered equivocal and may require additional testing, commonly using in situ hybridization (ISH) to determine whether the HER2 gene is amplified.

The exact interpretation should come from the pathology team and treating oncologist. See [how ER, PR and HER2 are tested](/blogs/er-pr-her2-breast-cancer-treatment-india) and [how diagnosis is built](/blogs/breast-cancer-diagnosis-tests-biopsy-er-pr-her2).
Why Is HER2 Testing Important?

HER2 status can change the treatment strategy significantly. A patient with HER2-positive disease may be considered for HER2-targeted treatment. A patient whose cancer is HER2-negative would generally not receive the same HER2-targeted regimen.
Therefore, a breast cancer diagnosis should not be based only on the tumour's location or stage. Doctors also consider its biological characteristics.
Important breast cancer markers include estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR) and HER2. These results help create an individualized treatment plan.
Can HER2-Positive Breast Cancer Also Be Hormone Receptor-Positive?
Yes. HER2 status and hormone receptor status are separate characteristics.
A breast cancer can be HER2-positive and ER-positive, HER2-positive and PR-positive, HER2-positive and ER/PR-positive, or HER2-positive and hormone receptor-negative.

This distinction matters because a patient with both HER2-positive and hormone receptor-positive disease may have a treatment plan involving both [HER2-targeted therapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Targeted-Therapy) and [endocrine therapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Hormone-Therapy).

- [Hormone Therapy Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Medical-Oncology/Hormone-Therapy)
- [Hormone Therapy Cost in India](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Hormone-Therapy)
How Is HER2-Positive Breast Cancer Treated?

blocks.alt: A patient with a surgeon, medical oncologist, radiation oncologist and cardiologist planning HER2-positive treatment
blocks.caption: Surgery, systemic HER2-directed treatment, radiation and cardiac monitoring often share one plan rather than working in isolation.

blocks.text: There is no single treatment plan for every HER2-positive breast cancer patient. Treatment depends on [cancer stage](/blogs/breast-cancer-stages-0-1-2-3-4), tumour size, lymph-node involvement, ER/PR status, HER2 status, whether the cancer is early-stage or metastatic, previous treatment, overall health and response to treatment.

Treatment may involve [surgery](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Lumpectomy), [chemotherapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Chemotherapy), [HER2-targeted therapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Targeted-Therapy), [radiation therapy](/costs/India/Radiation-Oncology/EBRT), [hormone therapy](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Hormone-Therapy) and other systemic treatments in selected situations.
[Ask which treatments apply in your case](/consult?treatment=Breast%20Cancer%20Treatment%20in%20India)
Treatment of Early-Stage HER2-Positive Breast Cancer

For early-stage HER2-positive breast cancer, treatment often involves a combination of local and systemic therapy. Depending on the case, treatment may begin with systemic therapy before surgery. This is called neoadjuvant therapy. See [treatment by stage](/blogs/breast-cancer-treatment-by-stage).
A simplified pathway could look like: Diagnosis → HER2 testing → Neoadjuvant treatment → Surgery → Additional treatment → Radiation/endocrine treatment where indicated.
However, the sequence is not identical for every patient. The treatment team determines the order based on tumour characteristics and the patient's clinical circumstances.
Why Is Treatment Sometimes Given Before Surgery?

For some HER2-positive breast cancers, doctors may recommend treatment before surgery. It can treat microscopic disease throughout the body early, reduce the size of the breast tumour, treat involved lymph nodes, provide information about how the cancer responds to treatment, and help guide treatment after surgery.
The pathology obtained during surgery can also provide information about whether residual cancer remains after preoperative treatment.
HER2-Targeted Therapy

blocks.alt: Patient receiving an infusion while a medical oncologist prepares HER2-targeted treatment
blocks.caption: HER2-targeted medicines may be given before surgery, after surgery, or for recurrent or metastatic disease.

blocks.text: HER2-targeted therapy is designed to interfere specifically with HER2-driven cancer biology. This differs from conventional chemotherapy.
Targeted medicines may be used before surgery, after surgery, for recurrent disease or for metastatic disease. The exact medicine and duration depend on the clinical setting.
Trastuzumab

Trastuzumab is one of the most established HER2-targeted medicines. It binds to the HER2 protein and interferes with HER2-related signalling. It may be used as part of treatment for HER2-positive breast cancer in different clinical settings.
Treatment may be administered intravenously or through another formulation depending on the available treatment and clinical situation.
Pertuzumab

Pertuzumab is another HER2-targeted medicine. In selected patients, it may be combined with trastuzumab and chemotherapy. This combination can be used in particular treatment settings, including some patients with higher-risk early-stage disease or advanced disease.
Other HER2-Targeted Treatments

HER2-directed treatment has expanded beyond trastuzumab and pertuzumab. Depending on the clinical situation, other HER2-directed medicines may include trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1), trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) and other HER2-directed agents.

These medicines are not interchangeable. Their use depends on stage, previous treatment, response to treatment, residual disease after preoperative treatment, metastatic disease, availability and clinical indication.

- [HER2-Targeted Therapy Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Medical-Oncology/Targeted-Therapy)
- [Targeted Therapy Cost in India](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Targeted-Therapy)

blocks.label: WhatsApp +91 90443 46292 about targeted therapy

blocks.text: What Is the Role of Chemotherapy?
Chemotherapy remains an important part of treatment for many HER2-positive breast cancers. However, HER2-targeted therapy and chemotherapy are different treatments.

Chemotherapy acts through mechanisms that damage rapidly dividing cancer cells. HER2-targeted medicines specifically interfere with HER2-driven signalling. They are often used together in appropriate treatment settings.

- [Chemotherapy Doctors in India](/doctors/India/Medical-Oncology/Chemotherapy)
- [Chemotherapy Cost in India](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Chemotherapy)

[Ask about chemotherapy timing](/consult?treatment=Chemotherapy) · [WhatsApp +91 90443 46292](https://wa.me/919044346292?text=Please%20advise%20whether%20chemotherapy%20is%20likely%20with%20my%20HER2-positive%20diagnosis.)
Does Every HER2-Positive Patient Need Chemotherapy?
Not necessarily. Treatment depends on the patient's individual cancer characteristics.

Factors that influence the decision may include tumour size, lymph-node status, stage, patient age and general health, hormone receptor status, risk of recurrence, treatment setting and other pathological findings.

Some small, early-stage HER2-positive cancers may be treated with less intensive regimens than larger or node-positive cancers. The appropriate treatment should be determined by the treating oncology team.
HER2-Positive Breast Cancer Surgery

Surgery remains an important component of treatment for many patients with localized HER2-positive breast cancer. Depending on the tumour and patient factors, surgery may include [breast-conserving surgery](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Lumpectomy), [mastectomy](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Mastectomy), sentinel lymph node biopsy and axillary lymph node surgery when indicated.

- [Breast-Conserving Surgery (Lumpectomy) in India](/doctors/India/Surgical-Oncology/Lumpectomy)
- [Mastectomy in India](/doctors/India/Surgical-Oncology/Mastectomy)
- [Nipple-Sparing Mastectomy](/doctors/India/Surgical-Oncology/Nipple-Sparing-Mastectomy)
Can HER2-Positive Patients Have Lumpectomy?
Yes. HER2-positive status by itself does not automatically mean that a patient needs a mastectomy. Some patients can undergo breast-conserving surgery when the tumour and breast anatomy are suitable.
The overall treatment usually also includes appropriate systemic therapy and, after breast-conserving surgery, [radiation therapy](/costs/India/Radiation-Oncology/EBRT) in most cases.
Can HER2-Positive Patients Have Mastectomy?

Yes. Mastectomy may be considered when the tumour is large relative to breast size, there are multiple areas of cancer, breast conservation is not appropriate, there are other clinical or genetic considerations, or the patient chooses mastectomy after discussing the options.

If reconstruction is desired, it may be performed immediately or later depending on the treatment plan. Explore [Breast Reconstruction in India](/costs/India/Surgical-Oncology/Breast-Reconstruction) and [reconstruction doctors](/doctors/India/Surgical-Oncology/Breast-Reconstruction).
What Is the Role of Radiation Therapy?

Radiation therapy may be recommended depending on the type of surgery and cancer characteristics. For patients undergoing breast-conserving surgery, radiation therapy is generally an important part of breast-conserving treatment.

After mastectomy, radiation may be recommended for selected patients based on tumour size, lymph-node involvement, other pathological findings and risk of recurrence. HER2-positive status alone does not determine whether radiation is required.
HER2-Positive Breast Cancer and Hormone Therapy
Some HER2-positive cancers are also hormone receptor-positive. If the cancer is ER-positive and/or PR-positive, endocrine therapy may be included in treatment.

This means a patient could potentially receive chemotherapy + HER2-targeted therapy + surgery + radiation + hormone therapy. But not every patient requires every treatment. Treatment should be individualized according to tumour biology and stage.
Treatment of HER2-Positive Metastatic Breast Cancer
Metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer is treated differently from localized disease. When breast cancer has spread to distant organs, systemic treatment becomes central to management.

Treatment may involve HER2-targeted medicines, chemotherapy, endocrine therapy for hormone receptor-positive disease, or other systemic therapies depending on previous treatment and the characteristics of the cancer. Treatment may change over time if the disease progresses or stops responding to a particular regimen.
What Happens If HER2-Positive Cancer Remains After Preoperative Treatment?
For some patients who receive treatment before surgery, pathology after surgery may show whether residual invasive cancer remains. This information can influence postoperative treatment.

For example, patients with residual HER2-positive disease after appropriate preoperative treatment may be considered for a different HER2-directed postoperative treatment rather than simply continuing the original regimen.
HER2-Positive Breast Cancer: Common Treatment Pathways
There is no universal pathway, but some examples include:

items: Early-stage disease: Diagnosis → HER2 testing → systemic therapy → surgery → additional systemic therapy ± radiation
HER2-positive and hormone receptor-positive: Diagnosis → HER2-directed treatment ± chemotherapy → surgery → radiation where indicated → endocrine therapy
Metastatic disease: Diagnosis of metastatic HER2-positive disease → systemic HER2-directed treatment → monitoring → subsequent therapy if disease progresses

blocks.text: These are simplified examples rather than treatment prescriptions.
How Is HER2-Positive Breast Cancer Monitored During Treatment?

blocks.alt: Clinician performing an echocardiogram on a clothed patient during HER2-targeted treatment
blocks.caption: Some HER2-targeted medicines can affect heart function, so cardiac assessment may be part of the monitoring plan.

blocks.text: Monitoring depends on the treatment regimen. Doctors may assess physical examination, blood tests, imaging, tumour response, treatment-related side effects and heart function when required by the HER2-directed medicine.
What Are the Side Effects of HER2-Targeted Therapy?

Side effects depend on the specific medicine and combination being used. Possible side effects may include fatigue, diarrhea, nausea, infusion-related reactions, reduced blood counts when combined with chemotherapy, and changes in heart function with some HER2-targeted medicines.

Not every patient experiences these effects. The combination of chemotherapy and HER2-targeted therapy can also make it difficult to determine which medicine is responsible for a particular symptom. Patients should report new or persistent symptoms to their oncology team.
Heart Monitoring During HER2-Targeted Treatment

Some HER2-targeted treatments can affect heart function. For this reason, doctors may assess cardiac function before and during treatment. Testing may include an echocardiogram or another appropriate cardiac assessment.

The exact monitoring schedule depends on the medicine being used, previous cardiac history, other risk factors, treatment duration and clinical findings. Patients should tell their oncologist about any history of heart disease or relevant cardiac treatment before starting therapy.
How Long Does HER2-Targeted Treatment Continue?
The duration varies according to the clinical setting. For many patients with early-stage HER2-positive breast cancer, HER2-directed treatment may continue for an extended period after surgery.

For metastatic disease, treatment may continue as long as it is controlling the cancer and side effects remain manageable, with changes made when clinically necessary. The exact duration should be determined by the treating oncologist.
HER2-Positive Breast Cancer Treatment Cost in India

The cost of treating HER2-positive breast cancer can vary significantly. Unlike a single surgical procedure, HER2-positive treatment may involve several months of systemic treatment and multiple components. See the [breast cancer treatment cost guide](/blogs/breast-cancer-treatment-cost-in-india) and [Targeted Therapy Cost in India](/costs/India/Medical-Oncology/Targeted-Therapy).

The total cost may include diagnostic tests, pathology and HER2 testing, imaging, surgery, chemotherapy, HER2-targeted medicines, radiation therapy, hospitalization or day-care treatment, blood tests, cardiac monitoring, supportive medicines and follow-up consultations.

The targeted medicines used can have a significant effect on the overall treatment cost. For this reason, it is not appropriate to provide one universal price for "HER2-positive breast cancer treatment." A patient-specific treatment plan and quotation are more useful.

What Determines the Cost of HER2-Targeted Treatment?

| Factor | Why it changes the cost |
| --- | --- |
| Medicine used | Different HER2-targeted medicines have different costs |
| Treatment duration | A longer course involves more doses |
| Combination therapy | HER2-targeted treatment may be combined with chemotherapy or other medicines |
| Route of administration | Some treatments require infusion facilities and monitoring |
| Hospital and day-care charges | Administration and monitoring add to the total |
| Additional investigations | Blood tests, imaging and cardiac monitoring may be required |
| Disease stage | Early-stage and metastatic pathways can differ substantially |
Why International Patients Should Get a Case-Specific Quote

For international patients, a general online price can be misleading because the treatment plan may change after pathology and imaging are reviewed. See the [international-patient guide](/blogs/breast-cancer-treatment-india-international-patients).

Before travelling to India, patients should ideally provide the biopsy report, histopathology, ER/PR results, HER2 report, imaging reports, previous treatment records, chemotherapy details, previous HER2-targeted treatment and current medicines.

[WhatsApp +91 90443 46292 your records before travel](https://wa.me/919044346292?text=I%20would%20like%20to%20send%20my%20HER2-positive%20breast%20cancer%20records%20for%20review%20before%20travelling%20to%20India.)
HER2-Positive Breast Cancer Treatment for International Patients in India

International patients may require coordination between several specialties. Depending on the case, the treatment team can include a breast surgical oncologist, medical oncologist, radiation oncologist, radiologist, pathologist, reconstructive surgeon and a cardiologist when clinically required.

Before travelling, patients should ask whether their pathology can be reviewed remotely. This can help clarify whether additional testing is required, whether surgery is likely, whether systemic treatment should begin first, the expected treatment sequence, the approximate duration of stay, and whether a second opinion is recommended.

Hospitals in [Delhi NCR](/hospitals/India/Delhi-NCR), [Mumbai](/hospitals/India/Mumbai), [Bengaluru](/hospitals/India/Bengaluru), [Chennai](/hospitals/India/Chennai) and [Hyderabad](/hospitals/India/Hyderabad) can confirm what to send.
Questions to Ask Your Oncologist

items: What is my HER2 test result?
Was my HER2 result confirmed by the appropriate testing method?
Is my cancer also ER- or PR-positive?
What is the stage of my cancer?
Do I need treatment before surgery?

How long will HER2-targeted treatment continue?
Will my heart function need monitoring?
What side effects should I watch for?
What will determine whether the treatment is working?

Should I obtain a second opinion?

blocks.text: Frequently Asked Questions
Is HER2-positive breast cancer curable?

The outlook depends on the stage and other characteristics of the cancer. Many patients with early-stage HER2-positive breast cancer receive treatment with curative intent. Metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer is managed differently and generally requires ongoing systemic treatment.
Is HER2-positive breast cancer aggressive?

HER2-positive breast cancer has distinct biological characteristics and can behave differently from HER2-negative disease. Importantly, effective HER2-targeted treatments have significantly changed how HER2-positive breast cancer is managed.
What is the main treatment for HER2-positive breast cancer?
There is no single treatment. Depending on the situation, treatment may include surgery, chemotherapy, HER2-targeted therapy, radiation therapy and hormone therapy.
Does HER2-positive always mean chemotherapy is required?
No. The need for chemotherapy depends on tumour size, stage, lymph-node involvement, patient factors and the overall treatment plan.
Can HER2-positive breast cancer be hormone receptor-positive?
Yes. A tumour can be both HER2-positive and ER/PR-positive.
Can HER2-positive breast cancer be treated without surgery?

Some patients with advanced or metastatic disease may not undergo breast surgery because systemic treatment is the primary approach. For localized disease, surgery is often an important component when medically appropriate.
What is trastuzumab?
Trastuzumab is a HER2-targeted medicine used to treat HER2-positive breast cancer in appropriate clinical settings.
What is pertuzumab?
Pertuzumab is another HER2-targeted medicine that may be combined with trastuzumab and chemotherapy in selected patients.
Does HER2-targeted treatment have side effects?
Yes. Side effects vary by medicine and combination. They can include fatigue, gastrointestinal symptoms, infusion reactions and, with some medicines, effects on heart function.
How is HER2 status determined?
HER2 is commonly assessed using immunohistochemistry. Equivocal results may require additional testing such as in situ hybridization.
How much does HER2-positive breast cancer treatment cost in India?
There is no fixed price. The cost depends on the stage, medicines, targeted therapy, chemotherapy, surgery, radiation, monitoring and treatment duration.
Can international patients receive HER2-targeted treatment in India?
Yes. International patients can seek evaluation and treatment in India. Their pathology and previous treatment records should ideally be reviewed before travel.
HER2-Positive Breast Cancer in India: Key Takeaways

HER2-positive breast cancer is defined by specific biological characteristics identified through tumour testing. Treatment may involve HER2-targeted therapy, chemotherapy, surgery, radiation therapy, hormone therapy when the cancer is hormone receptor-positive, and other systemic treatments in selected situations.

The treatment plan depends on stage, HER2 status, ER/PR status, tumour characteristics, previous treatment and overall health. For international patients, obtaining a pathology review and treatment plan before travelling can help clarify the expected treatment sequence and potential costs.

This guide explains how international patients can approach [Breast Cancer Treatment in India](/treatments/breast-cancer-treatment-in-india), from [pre-travel diagnosis review](/blogs/breast-cancer-diagnosis-tests-biopsy-er-pr-her2) through [treatment by stage](/blogs/breast-cancer-treatment-by-stage) and [follow-up](/blogs/breast-cancer-treatment-cost-in-india).
